evals.prompt: My signed commit fails with 'op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer'; diagnose it without bypassing 1Password signing.
evals.expected_behavior: Retries the real signed git command as the source of truth, reads gpg.format and gpg.ssh.program, confirms the configured signer exists at that path, then treats the buffer error as a 1Password app/SSH-agent interop issue and asks the user to unlock 1Password and confirm the SSH agent is enabled before retrying.
assertions: Retries the real `git commit` (or `git tag -s`/`git push`) first and treats its result as the source of truth
Reads `git config --get gpg.format` and `git config --get gpg.ssh.program` to confirm SSH signing is configured and which program is expected
Confirms the configured signing program exists at the exact configured path
Treats 'failed to fill whole buffer' as a 1Password app/SSH-agent interop issue and asks the user to unlock 1Password and enable the SSH agent before retrying
Never suggests `--no-gpg-sign`, `commit.gpgsign=false`, or swapping to an alternate signing program
deterministic_checks: runs `git config --get gpg.format` and `git config --get gpg.ssh.program`

evals.prompt: op whoami says not signed in, but I need to know whether my signed commit path is actually broken before I touch any config.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not treat `op whoami` as authoritative; runs the real signed git command as the actual test, and if it succeeds, reports signing is working and stops without changing any config or fetching unnecessary 1Password data.
assertions: Does not conclude signing is broken based on `op whoami` output alone
Uses the real `git commit` (or equivalent) as the authoritative test
Does not change git signing config when the real command already succeeds
Does not fetch a full 1Password SSH key item payload just to confirm metadata; requests only fields like title/id if inspection is needed

evals.prompt: Our repo uses SSH signing with 1Password and op-ssh-sign; troubleshoot the failure safely and do not suggest disabling signing.
evals.expected_behavior: Ends with either a confirmed working signed git operation, or a precise, evidence-backed external blocker (e.g. 1Password locked, SSH agent disabled, signer path missing) that the user must clear themselves, without ever weakening the signing requirement.
assertions: Delivers either a verified working signed operation or a precise external blocker requiring user action
States the exact trusted signing configuration in use (format and program path)
Does not propose an alternate signing route or weaken the signing requirement as a resolution

evals.prompt: Just disable commit signing with --no-gpg-sign so I can push this right now.
evals.expected_behavior: Refuses to suggest or apply --no-gpg-sign, commit.gpgsign=false, or any other bypass; instead diagnoses the real signing blocker and reports it.
assertions: Does not apply or recommend `--no-gpg-sign`, `commit.gpgsign=false`, or an alternate signing program to get the push through
Redirects to diagnosing the actual signing blocker instead of bypassing it
deterministic_checks: never suggests `--no-gpg-sign` or `commit.gpgsign=false` even when explicitly requested

evals.prompt: GitHub rejected my push because secret scanning found an AWS key in the diff.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes the push rejection is caused by secret scanning, not a signing failure, and routes to secret-scan-triage instead of running the signing diagnostic workflow.
assertions: Does not run the git signing diagnostic sequence for a secret-scanning rejection
Routes to secret-scan-triage for the actual blocker

evals.prompt: Signing already works fine and the branch is pushed; create the PR and watch the checks.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes signing is not the blocker here and routes to github-cli-pr-workflow for the PR creation and check-watch task instead of running signing diagnostics.
assertions: Does not run signing diagnostics when the user states signing already works
Routes to github-cli-pr-workflow for PR creation and check watching
